summary.name: Psono
summary.one_liner: Psono is an open-source, self-hosted password manager for companies that encrypts vault data on the client and supports encrypted team sharing.
keywords: browser password manager chrome firefox edge
use_cases: Storing team credentials on company servers
Sharing passwords securely within a team
Running a password vault behind a corporate firewall
Keeping vault data off third-party infrastructure
summary.what_it_does: Psono is a password manager that can be self-hosted on a company's own servers, with all components runnable in-house. Vault data is encrypted on the client before it is sent to the server, and the server stores only encrypted data. It supports encrypted sharing of credentials with team members and allows passwords to be exported. The page states the full codebase is publicly auditable. Clients are described for macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS, and Android, with use in Chrome, Firefox, and Edge and sync across devices.
notable: Client-side encryption before data reaches the server
Fully self-hostable with publicly auditable source code (Apache-2.0)
Enterprise features such as SAML, LDAP, audit logs and compliance policies
Encrypted sharing and export of passwords
caveats: Professional support and SLAs require contacting the vendor for a quote
Pricing tiers are referenced but not detailed on the page
Self-hosting means the organization runs and maintains the server
